title: Screw the four legs onto a side table (two Frankas, operational-space control)
text:
An IKEA-style side table, partly assembled, lying on a sturdy waist-high workbench. The free-standing tabletop slab (~0.55 x 0.55 m, 5 cm thick) carries 4 upright threaded studs at its corners (xy = (+0.25, +0.25), (-0.25, +0.25), (+0.25, -0.25), (-0.25, -0.25) m, relative to the slab centre). 4 loose legs — each a threaded nut on a graspable cylindrical shaft — lie on their side in a row near the centre of the workbench, ready to be picked up and fitted.
Goal: screw every leg down onto its stud (turn it clockwise while pressing down) until it seats. A seated leg locks in place. The table is assembled once all 4 legs are seated.
success: Success, exactly: at the end of the run, each of the 4 legs is screwed onto a stud of the tabletop slab: in the slab's own frame (origin at the centre of the slab's top face, the face carrying the studs; up = that face's normal), the point on the leg's axis at its threaded-nut end [the leg's origin] is at most 12 mm above the slab's top face (a leg sitting on top of a stud is at 26 mm), within 20 mm, in the slab plane, of one of the stud axes at (±0.25, ±0.25) m from the slab centre, and the leg's long axis, nut end to shaft end, is within 10° of the slab's up direction. Any leg may use any stud; the slab may have moved. Not true at the start (the legs lie on the workbench). [success() = seated().all(); leg origin = its nut body origin]
